question.text: Intramolecular forces between n-hexane and n-heptane are nearly same as between hexane and heptane individually. When these two are mixed, which of the following is not true about the solution formed?

options.text: It obeys Raoult's law, i.e.  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>  and  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow></msub></math>  is zero

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow></msub></math>  is zero

solution.text: n-hexane and n-heptane form an ideal solution so here azeotropic mixture is not possible.
